mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4%, or inflation-adjusted discount rates show no significant effect on SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs coinciding with a falling UNRATE (unemployment rate) suggests labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises ≥50,000 and UNRATE falls in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60-day window when both conditions hold, or correlation between the two proxies is below 0.6.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (real personal consumption) exceeding 2% signals weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as investors anticipate profit-taking.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative in at least 70% of such demand weakness episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 over two consecutive months indicates supply-side constraints, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as demand outpaces supply.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day returns when INDPRO contracts for two months, or alternative supply metrics show no correlation.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive as lower rates encourage equity investment and corporate financing.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the trigger is met, or alternative monetary indicators contradict the policy stance.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% in the prior month accompanied by a rise in HOUST (home sales) suggests labor market loosening and consumer confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and HOUST rises in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when both proxies move in the predicted direction, or interaction p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly RSAFS (retail sales) exceeding 10,000 million dollars in a period of rising CPIAUCSL (inflation) indicates demand is growing faster than prices, which tends to produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to profit margin compression.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises and RSAFS exceeds 10,000M in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when the interaction is present, or alternative inflation measures show no effect.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE remains above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to persistent labor market slack and reduced investment incentives.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in more than 80% of such episodes, or alternative supply/labor indicators contradict the signal.
